title: Machine-learning-guided Fe₂P-type alloys reach cryogenic magnetocaloric temperatures without rare earths
summary: An artificial neural network trained on reported experimental compositions guided optimization of Fe₂P-type Mn–Fe–P–Si alloys for sub-77 K magnetocaloric use. Experiments measured a 97 K transition for Mn₁.₇₀Fe₀.₃₀P₀.₆₃Si₀.₃₇ at 1 T; replacing a small fraction of Fe with Co lowered the transition to 73 K. The Co-containing composition showed a 7.5 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ magnetic entropy change and a 1.4 K reversible adiabatic temperature change under a 0–5 T field.
ai_technology: Artificial neural network trained on a curated, literature-mined dataset of experimental Fe₂P-type magnetocaloric compounds
organization: National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS); South China Normal University

evidence.tested: An artificial neural network trained on reported experimental compositions guided optimization of Fe₂P-type Mn–Fe–P–Si alloys for sub-77 K magnetocaloric use.
evidence.unknown: The reported compositions are rare-earth-free but still contain transition metals and phosphorus/silicon; results characterize laboratory alloys and do not establish a working hydrogen-liquefaction refrigerator. The 73 K transition requires Co substitution and is reported with a modest reduction in magnetization. The 1.4 K reversible adiabatic change is measured over 0–5 T; stated performance and operating window should not be generalized beyond the investigated alloys.
evidence.ai_role: The team mined published experimental composition/property results to train an artificial neural network for composition optimization toward lower transition temperatures. Predictions guided selection of Mn₁.₇₀Fe₀.₃₀P₀.₆₃Si₀.₃₇, then a minor Co-for-Fe substitution was tested experimentally to reduce its transition temperature below 77 K. AI guided composition selection; the reported magnetic and caloric properties came from measurements on synthesized samples.
